setup: The application is installed and launched on a workstation, and a PDF document is available in the user's file system.
action: The user opens the application from the desktop and navigates to the main tool window.
expected_observation: A free graphical PDF manipulation tool interface is displayed, with visible controls for working with PDF documents.

setup: A source PDF file exists in a folder, and a separate output location is available for generated documents.
action: The user performs a PDF operation such as splitting or rotating the source file and saves the result.
expected_observation: The generated output file reflects the requested changes, and the original source PDF remains unchanged in its original location and content.

setup: The application is available both as a graphical interface and a command-line utility, and a sample PDF document is present for processing.
action: The user completes one PDF task through the graphical interface and submits an equivalent task through the command line.
expected_observation: The same type of PDF manipulation can be completed successfully in both modes, supporting manual visual use and repeatable command-line execution.

setup: A casual user is viewing the graphical interface, and an automation user has access to the command-line interface on the same system.
action: The casual user splits a PDF through the visual interface, while the automation user runs a recurring PDF job from the command line.
expected_observation: Both usage styles are supported: the graphical workflow is usable for everyday hands-on PDF tasks, and the command-line workflow is suitable for automated or repeated jobs.

setup: A multi-page PDF document is loaded into the application.
action: The user chooses to split the PDF into separate output files by page range or individual pages.
expected_observation: The system creates the requested split PDF files, each containing only the selected portion of the original document.

setup: Two or more PDF files, or selected sections from PDFs, are available for combination.
action: The user selects the files or sections and initiates a merge operation.
expected_observation: The system produces a single merged PDF containing the selected content in the chosen order.

setup: A PDF document with multiple pages is open in the application.
action: The user selects a subset of pages to extract into a new document.
expected_observation: The system generates a new PDF containing only the chosen pages, preserving their original content and order.

setup: A PDF document with pages in a known orientation is loaded into the tool.
action: The user rotates one or more selected pages by a specified angle and saves the result.
expected_observation: The affected pages are saved in the new orientation, and the output PDF displays those pages rotated as requested.

setup: A PDF document containing several pages is open and its page order is visible.
action: The user moves selected pages to new positions within the document and applies the change.
expected_observation: The resulting PDF reflects the revised page sequence exactly as arranged by the user.

setup: Two source PDFs with pages intended for alternating sequence are available for processing.
action: The user configures the documents so that pages are taken alternately from each source and starts the operation.
expected_observation: The output document contains pages interleaved from the different source PDFs in the specified alternating order.

setup: The visual composition workspace is open, and the user has one or more PDF pages or documents ready to place on a new document layout.
action: The user arranges the selected content visually on the composition canvas and saves the composed document.
expected_observation: A new PDF is created matching the visual layout defined by the user, with the arranged content placed as composed.

setup: A user has configured a PDF processing workflow in the application, including selected files and operation settings.
action: The user saves the current workspace or job configuration for later reuse.
expected_observation: The system stores the setup as a reusable environment that can be reopened and applied again without rebuilding the configuration from scratch.

setup: A repeatable PDF task is available, and the command-line interface can access the required source files and output location.
action: The user runs the PDF operation from the command line with the necessary parameters.
expected_observation: The system executes the requested PDF task without requiring the graphical interface, making the operation suitable for automation and recurring use.
